description: task-c2 — Microsoft Intune (MDM) weaponized for endpoint persistence, where the malicious app one user noticed is only the symptom. Over a change-freeze weekend an intruder with Intune-admin access planted a malicious required Win32 app on the Design team, dropped a broad security-weakening configuration profile, and — the deciding move — TAMPERED the trusted, long-standing 'Corporate Windows Security Baseline' (assigned to all devices): disabled Defender real-time protection and added a Defender folder exclusion for the malware's payload directory (C:\ProgramData\VireoSync). Removing the app and quarantining the reported device is necessary but INSUFFICIENT: while the baseline stays tampered, every Windows endpoint runs with real-time protection off and a carve-out that lets the payload execute undetected. 6 counted assertions (all fail on the untouched world). Planted-object checks are neutralization-agnostic (an app/profile counts as remediated if deleted, unassigned, or — for apps — set to uninstall intent), so no exact mechanism is demanded. No format/bookkeeping checks, no untouched-data guards, no runbook. Escalation is destination-agnostic and graded on intent, not wording.
